evaluation:
Helpful Facts:

  • Headache Characteristics: Severe, unilateral, throbbing/pulsating quality. This aligns with typical migraine headache descriptions.
  • Exacerbating Factors: Worsened by movement (physical activity). This is a common feature of migraine.
  • Associated Symptoms: Nausea, near-emesis, photophobia (sensitivity to light), and phonophobia (sensitivity to sound). These are classic migraine-associated symptoms.
  • Aura: Reports visual aura (flashing lights, zigzags, blind spots) preceding the headache. This is a key feature of migraine with aura.
  • Recurrence: History of similar headaches occurring a few times per year. This suggests a recurrent headache disorder, consistent with migraine.
  • Worsening Factors: Worsening symptoms with strong smells (osmophobia) and fatigue. These are known migraine triggers or exacerbating factors.
  • Negative Symptoms (Pertinent Negatives): Denies fever and chills (makes infectious causes less likely), denies recent head/neck injury (rules out traumatic causes), denies recent travel or sick contacts (reduces likelihood of infectious causes).
  • Duration: Onset approximately two days ago, suggesting a duration that fits within a migraine episode.
  • Dysphasia and Neck Stiffness: While less typical, these symptoms were reported concurrently and could be part of a complex migraine presentation or warrant further investigation.

What wasn't covered but would be helpful:

  • Family History: Inquiring about a family history of migraines is crucial, as migraines often have a genetic component.
  • Detailed Aura Description: While aura is mentioned, more detail (duration of aura, specific sequence of symptoms, whether it's always the same) would be helpful.
  • Headache Duration: The report states onset was two days ago, but the *duration* of the current headache episode is not specified (e.g., has it been continuous for 2 days, or episodic?).
  • Pain Scale: A numerical pain scale rating (e.g., 1-10) would quantify the severity.
  • Impact on Function: How does the headache affect daily activities (work, school, social life)? This helps assess the disability caused by the headaches.
  • Previous Treatments/Effectiveness: Although the patient denies taking medication *for this headache*, asking about previous treatments for similar headaches and their effectiveness (or lack thereof) would be valuable.
  • Specific Triggers: While the patient denies *identifying* specific triggers, a more detailed exploration of potential triggers (dietary, hormonal, stress, sleep patterns) might reveal patterns.
  • Neurological Exam Findings (if available): Although this is a pre-visit report, any prior neurological exam findings (even if normal) would be helpful context.
  • Associated Symptoms (Further Detail): Any associated dizziness, vertigo, or changes in vision *during* the headache (beyond the aura) could be relevant.
  • Menstrual History (if applicable): For female patients, inquiring about the relationship between headaches and the menstrual cycle (menstrual migraine) is important.
  • Review of Systems (Broader): A more comprehensive review of systems might uncover other relevant symptoms or comorbidities.
